info.name: Send Transactions API
info.description:
REST API collection for SEND_TXN_OWNER schema.
Base URL and tranId are collection variables — edit them under the Variables tab.

variable.description: Dedicated id for the metadata-driven (v2) folder so v1 and v2 examples don't collide.
A client-supplied address id used in the addr_dtl merge-and-prune demo. When the service sees an explicit id it MERGEs that row instead of generating a new UUID.

item.name: Metadata-Driven (v2) API
item.description:
Tests for the new generic, YAML-metadata-driven endpoints at /api/v2/*.

The routes are:
  PUT    /api/v2/{alias}/{id}    upsert (parent + children if alias is a root table)
  GET    /api/v2/{alias}/{id}    fetch with nested children
  GET    /api/v2/{alias}         paginated parent rows (no children)
  DELETE /api/v2/{alias}/{id}    cascade-delete
  GET    /api/v2/_metadata       list all loaded tables
  GET    /api/v2/_metadata/{alias}   describe one table

Aliases come from the YAML files under src/main/resources/metadata/:
  send-transactions  send-tran-dtl  send-recip-dtl  send-tran-addr-dtl

Adding a new column = one line in YAML + DDL change. No Java changes.

request.description: Returns the column metadata for every loaded YAML. Mitigation for loss-of-Swagger after the move to Map<String,Object> payloads.
Returns the columns, child references, audit/CLOB/converter flags for a single table — useful for client codegen or API doc generation.
Look for clob:true on bncGtwyRqst / bncGtwyResp / origRqstPyld / origRespPyld.
Inserts the parent only. The response is a JSON Map (not a typed POJO) shaped from the metadata column list.

request.description:
Demonstrates every special case in one call:
  - CLOB via clob:true → TO_CLOB CASE WHEN (bncGtwyRqst, bncGtwyResp, origRqstPyld, origRespPyld, sendGovtIdUri)
  - DATE round-trip (sendDob, recipDob)
  - NUMBER(1,0) ↔ Boolean via converter:BOOLEAN_AS_INT (nonFinTxn: true)
  - 1:1 child upsert (tranDtl, recipDtl)
  - 1:many child MERGE with one client-supplied id (addrDtl[0]) and one auto-UUID (addrDtl[1])
  - Audit columns SYSTIMESTAMP-populated server-side

Run the GET request next to see the full nested graph reflected back.

item.name: v2-U3. Null-guard demo (only tranAmt updated, others preserved)

request.description:
Run AFTER v2-U2.

Sends explicit nulls for curStat and ntwrkCd. The generated MERGE uses COALESCE(:p, t.COL) — so the existing non-null values in the DB (curStat=COMPLETED, ntwrkCd=MASTERCARD from v2-U2) survive. Only tranAmt changes.

Required fields (tranCrteDt, tranType) must still be sent because metadata validator enforces required on every upsert.

Writes ~1.5 KB into the CLOB column BNC_GTWY_RQST via the auto-generated  CASE WHEN :p IS NOT NULL THEN TO_CLOB(:p) ELSE t.COL END  pattern. The parameter is bound as Types.VARCHAR — Oracle promotes it to CLOB.

GET v2-Q1 should return the same string verbatim.

request.description:
Run AFTER v2-U2 (which created 2 addresses, one with explicit id={{addrIdV2}}, one auto-UUID).

This request sends only the explicit-id address. The service:
  1. MERGEs the explicit-id row (updates stLine1)
  2. Collects keepIds = [{{addrIdV2}}]
  3. DELETEs every other address for this tranId NOT IN keepIds — so the auto-UUID one is removed.

A following GET will show exactly 1 address.

item.name: v2-U6. addr_dtl empty list → delete all

request.description: Empty array semantics: every SEND_TRAN_ADDR_DTL row for this tranId is deleted. A following GET will show addrDtl: [].
When tranDtl / recipDtl / addrDtl keys are absent (not just null) the service leaves those child rows alone. Use the GET that follows to confirm the existing children survive.

item.name: v2-Q1. GET by ID - Full Graph

request.description:
Response is a Map<String,Object> assembled from the YAML metadata:
  - parent columns at the root
  - tranDtl   → nested Map (or null)
  - recipDtl  → nested Map (or null)
  - addrDtl   → array of Maps

Field order follows the YAML column order (LinkedHashMap).
Paginated parent-only list (no child data). Same PagedResponse shape as v1, with first/last flags.
Validated by @Min(0) on page and @Min(1)@Max(100) on size.

item.name: Direct Child-Table Access
item.description: Because every table is registered with its own alias, child tables are addressable on their own — useful for ops queries and partial updates that don't need to walk through the parent.

request.description: SEND_TRAN_DTL has PK = FK = TRAN_ID. The {id} path variable is the tranId.
Returns the SEND_RECIP_DTL row (sender + recipient PII, DOBs as ISO yyyy-MM-dd).

item.name: v2-C3. GET single address by its UUID

request.description: SEND_TRAN_ADDR_DTL has a per-row PK (ID). Use the id returned in v2-Q1's addrDtl[] array. The collection variable {{addrIdV2}} is set to the fixed id used in v2-U2.

item.name: v2-C4. PATCH a single address directly (null-guard)

request.description: Direct child-row MERGE. Only addrStat + updtUserNam change; all other fields are preserved by the COALESCE null-guard. Note: tranId (FK) and id (PK) are required by the metadata so they must be sent.
Service-side cascade: addrDtl → tranDtl → recipDtl → parent (because the DDL has no ON DELETE CASCADE). Returns 204.
MetadataValidator enforces required:true from YAML. Same 400 JSON shape (fieldErrors map) as v1's @NotBlank failure — the global handler treats them identically.
Expect 400 with fieldErrors.tranCrteDt = "must not be null".
tranType is VARCHAR2(10) in DDL and maxLength:10 in YAML. Expect 400 with fieldErrors.tranType = "must not exceed 10 characters". No DB call is made.

item.name: v2-E4. 400 - Child tranDtl missing required tranCrteDt

request.description: Validation runs per section. Expect 400 on the child's required:true tranCrteDt field.
Bean Validation on the controller, not metadata-driven. Returns 400 with ConstraintViolationException shape.
Returns 404 with the same ErrorResponse shape (UTC timestamp + traceId from MDC) as v1.

MetadataRegistry.require throws IllegalArgumentException for an unknown alias. Caught by the generic exception handler — 500 with a masked message ("An unexpected error occurred"). Real error visible in server logs.
